captive_summary: RE-VERIFY, OVERTURNS PRE-EXISTING TRUE. Chana LNG Terminal is an onshore LNG import/storage facility with pipelines built specifically to feed the adjacent Songkhla Chana 1.7 GW gas-fired combined-cycle power plant (KOWEPO/TPIPP/KOGAS JV, signed March 2021), whose electricity output is sold entirely to EGAT (the national grid), not consumed on-site by the terminal. This is the classic direction-test case: the terminal supplies gas OUT to an external power plant (already correctly captured in GEM's PowerPlantsSupplied = 'Songkhla Chana power station'); it is not powered BY a captive plant. No source anywhere describes on-site captive generation for the LNG terminal itself.

The power plant will be run for 25 years after construction and sell electricity to the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand' -- i.e. the LNG terminal operation is organizationally and physically separate from the power-generation operation, with output exported to the grid, not consumed captively by the terminal. Existing GEM CaptiveGasPower [ref] field was empty (no citation was ever attached to the pre-existing True), and no independent source found in this pass supports on-site captive generation at the terminal -- the pre-existing True appears to be a direction-test data error conflating 'terminal supplies an adjacent power plant' with 'terminal has captive power'.
